subject: Physics
description: SI units, instruments for measuring various quantities

questions.stem: The SI unit of FORCE is:
questions.explanation: Force — Newton (N) = kg·m/s². Joule — energy. Watt — power (J/s). Pascal — pressure (N/m²).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: Match the INSTRUMENT with what it MEASURES. A. Barometer.  B. Hygrometer.  C. Anemometer.  D. Lactometer. List-II: 1. Atmospheric pressure.  2. Humidity.  3. Wind speed.  4. Purity of milk.
questions.explanation: Barometer — atmospheric pressure (Torricelli). Hygrometer — humidity. Anemometer — wind speed. Lactometer — density of milk (purity). Other favourites: sphygmomanometer (BP), seismograph (earthquakes), galvanometer (small electric current).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The unit used to measure INTENSITY OF SOUND is:
questions.explanation: Decibel — logarithmic unit of sound intensity. Hertz — frequency. Watt — power. Candela — luminous intensity (light). Normal conversation: ~60 dB; rock concert: ~110 dB; jet engine: ~140 dB; pain threshold: ~130 dB.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: 1 HP (mechanical, 'imperial') = 745.7 W ≈ 746 W. Metric HP ≈ 735.5 W. Electric-motor ratings usually state HP in mechanical units. 1 kW = 1.341 HP.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The base SI unit for LUMINOUS INTENSITY is:
questions.explanation: Seven SI base units: metre (length), kilogram (mass), second (time), ampere (current), kelvin (temperature), mole (amount of substance), candela (luminous intensity). Lux and lumen are derived units (lumen = luminous flux; lux = illuminance = lumen/m²).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: LIGHT YEAR is a unit of:
questions.explanation: 1 light year = distance light travels in 1 year in vacuum ≈ 9.46 × 10¹² km. Despite the word 'year', it is DISTANCE. Classic trap. Other astronomical units: 1 AU = Earth-Sun distance ≈ 150 million km; 1 parsec ≈ 3.26 light years.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The instrument used to measure BLOOD PRESSURE is a:
questions.explanation: Sphygmomanometer ('sphygmos' = pulse, Greek). Stethoscope is used to LISTEN to heart sounds while taking BP, but doesn't measure the pressure itself. Output in mmHg — normal ~120/80.
questions.subject: Physics
